JUST IN: University of the Philippines Manila Chancellor Michael Tee has officially endorsed the Black Friday Protest after the University Student Council (USC) sent him a letter today, September 11.

This was preceded by the endorsement of the Black Friday protest mobilization by College of Arts and Sciences (CAS) Dean Ma. Theresa De Guzman, which will be led by the CAS Student Council (CASSC) and other organizations within the college.

The said college-wide walkout is set at 11:30 a.m., while the white colleges are also expected to follow from their respective buildings at Pedro Gil to CAS by 12 nn.

“[We] call on the entire UP Manila community to take part in the collective action against corruption and impunity, and to stand firm for transparency and accountability,” USC said on a Facebook post.

#KurakotManagot

data.raw_text:
READ: In a statement, UP President Angelo Jimenez expressed support for the brewing public outcry against anomalous flood control and infrastructure projects, as numerous mobilizations continue to spring up across Metro Manila.

Participants of these demonstrations have called to strengthen mechanisms for transparency as well as purge branches of government of corruption. These protests have emerged amid several public officials’ calls for peaceful means of protest.

The president also stressed the importance of harnessing education to solve problems within the country and the state.

“We shall employ all legal means to ensure full accountability, in fulfilment of our continuing duty to serve the Filipino people,” Jimenez wrote.

Photo from the UP Office of the President

data.raw_text:
[3:56PM] #AlausaIkeja #TrafficUpdate 

There is steady movement on Obafemi Awolowo Way, covering Shopping Mall, Coca-Cola Junction, Radio, Allen Junction, and Balogun. However, a slight slowdown is observed approaching Olowu, as vehicles turn towards the bridge, with minor delays caused by vehicle influx. The return journey along this axis remains smooth.

On Lateef Jakande Road, vehicular movement is fast from Coca-Cola through LTV 8, Cadbury, and Wemco Junction up to Omole Roundabout. Similarly, traffic along Aromire inward Adeniyi Jones is moving well, aside from slight delays at traffic signal light alternation points. The return journey is also smooth, although traffic builds slightly when approaching Allen Junction.

The entire stretch of Mobolaji Johnson Avenue, from Old Tollgate through 7Up Gate and Billings Way to the Alausa Intersection, is free-flowing. Movement along Dr. Nurudeen Olowopopo, connecting to Otedola underneath the bridge, is also smooth.

No impediments have been sighted, and traffic control structures remain on ground for adequate management. 

#FollowLASTMA

[4:35PM] #PWD #TraffiCUpdate 

Vehicular movement inward Bolade Intersection through Oshodi by Brown Junction is experiencing slow traffic at the moment, caused by vehicles entering Arena Shopping Mall. However, there is no cause for concern as traffic personnel are on ground managing the situation.

Traffic flow remains smooth around Ladipo, Shogunle, PWD, and Airport Turning, both ascending and descending the overpass and underpass, and movement is equally good from Ikeja Lagos through Ile Zik, Mongoro, and Cement down to the Dopemu underbridge. The return journey from Pako, connecting Dopemu underbridge and National, is also moving well.

PWD inward Bolade Intersection is generally clear, with only slight delays when approaching Bolade Junction due to traffic alternation. Traffic officers remain on ground to ensure smooth operations, and no impediments have been recorded at this time.

#FollowLASTMA
